change.title: ao-replay/9036
change.description:
feat(telemetry): break slow launches and frozen frames into named steps
fix(e2e): stub launchSteps in the fake desktop bridge
change.author: ronish

findings.title: Docs say only `first` and `cold` launches carry main's steps; `update` launches carry them too
findings.body: The renderer attaches steps when `start.kind === "cold"` (frontend/src/renderer/lib/launch-telemetry.ts:135), and `update` is a cold launch whose `launch_kind` was rewritten in `readLaunchKind` (line 57). So an `update` launch also sends `to_app_ready_ms`, `to_window_shown_ms`, `to_server_spawn_ms`, `to_server_ready_ms` and `server_reused`. The doc here (line 928), the table row (line 914), and the comment on `LAUNCH_STEP_PROPERTIES` in performance-telemetry-properties.ts all say "first or cold". Someone filtering dashboards by `launch_kind` would conclude update launches have no steps. The new tests cover `first` and `warm` only; none covers `update` with steps.

findings.title: `startup_ms` is measured from the start of `Run`, not from the daemon process starting
findings.body: The doc says `startup_ms` is "the milliseconds from the daemon process starting". The clock starts at `startedAt := time.Now()` (backend/internal/daemon/daemon.go:205), after `config.Load`, `stabilizeWorkingDirectory` and `lifecyclelog.Open` (daemon.go:177-204), and after Go runtime init. The startup_timing.go comment correctly says "from Run". Because the desktop's `to_server_ready_ms` and `startup_ms` will be compared on dashboards, the doc should say "from the start of the daemon's startup routine" so a residual gap isn't read as unexplained.

findings.title: The steps IPC runs after the usable-wait race and the pagehide handler are gone, with no bound of its own
findings.body: `launchProperties` bounds the wait with the race at lines 117-130, then removes the `pagehide` listener (line 132) and awaits `readLaunchSteps()` (line 135). That IPC call is outside both the 60 s bound and the close-time handoff. If the window closes during this await (normally a few ms, longer if main is busy at startup), the event is lost: `sendOnClose` is no longer registered and a page-lifetime promise is dropped. Before this change the properties were computed synchronously after the race, so this gap did not exist. Fix: read the steps before the race, or in parallel with it (cold launch only), so the `pagehide` handler can include them, or race the IPC with a short timeout.

findings.title: The `serverReused` derivation in the `telemetry:launchSteps` handler is untested
findings.body: `serverReused = spawned === undefined || spawned > ready` (main.ts:3739-3744) decides whether a launch attached to an existing daemon. It depends on mark order and on `daemonSpawned` being set at line 2700, before the `spawn` call (and so also when `spawn` throws synchronously at line 2711, which leaves a stale first-time mark because marks keep their first value). The handler is inline in `ipcMain.handle`, so no test covers reused, spawned, or restart-after-ready. Extracting it into a pure function next to `createLaunchTiming` would allow a unit test. The test only checks `marks()`.

contracts.action: New IPC `telemetry:launchSteps` returning main-process launch marks to the shell renderer
contracts.equivalent_path: `telemetry:takeLaunchStart` (main.ts:~3722-3730) and `telemetry:takeResourceSummary` (main.ts:3747) check `trustedShellWebContents.get(event.sender.id) !== event.sender` and return null; the new handler does the same.
contracts.before_after: Before: the renderer only got `startedAtMs`/kind. After: on a cold launch the renderer also fetches marks (appReady, windowShown, daemonSpawned, daemonReady) and derives `serverReused`. Unlike takeLaunchStart it is not consumed once, so repeated calls return the same marks (first-time-wins).
contracts.visible_effect: Extra properties on ao.launches.timed; nothing user-visible.
contracts.failure_mode: Untrusted sender gets null, no steps. A rejection is caught in readLaunchSteps and the event is sent without steps. The IPC await sits outside the usable-wait race and the pagehide handoff (launch-telemetry.ts:132-135), so a window closed during it loses the event (reported as a finding).

contracts.action: Detect first run by `existsSync(<dataDir>/ao.db)` at main module load and mark the cold launch `firstRun`
contracts.equivalent_path: The daemon creates `ao.db` in `storage/sqlite/db.go:60-67` when it opens the store; the desktop reads before spawning/adopting the daemon.
contracts.before_after: Before: first runs were reported as `cold`. After: `launch_kind: first`. `readLaunchKind` still writes the version key to localStorage before returning, so the next launch is `cold`.
contracts.failure_mode: A data dir whose database was deleted reads as first run. The existsSync is synchronous and cheap at module load, and a throw is not possible for a plain existence check.

contracts.action: Daemon emits `ao.daemon.ready` in the RunWithReady callback and `ao.daemon.startup_reconciled` from the background restore goroutine
contracts.equivalent_path: Other daemon telemetry goes through `telemetrySink.Emit` with a payload filtered by `remotePayloadAllowlist` (posthog.go:865-890).
contracts.before_after: Before: no startup timing. After: two events with int64 ms payloads. Allowlist entries and a coverage test were added, and `sanitizeRemoteValue` passes int64 through.
contracts.visible_effect: None for users; the daemon startup path gains a non-blocking Emit (PostHogSink.Emit drops when the queue is full for non-usage events).
contracts.failure_mode: Emit cannot block the ready callback (default branch, posthog.go:542-547). The `restore` steps struct is touched only by its own goroutine. The event is skipped when ctx is cancelled during restore.

contracts.action: Long-frame summaries now record entry-point names and app bundle names and bump the window format to version 3
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous `recordLongFrame` credited script time by invoker type only; the old persisted version 2 window is discarded by `loadState`.
contracts.before_after: Before: causes by invoker type, `other`. After: phase split (unlisted, frame-callbacks, forced-layout, rendering), per-cause `_ms` properties, top invoker and top bundle. Names pass `invokerName`/`bundleName` before being kept, and again on load and again in the sanitizer, so URLs, ids and attributes do not reach the event. I checked the worked examples in the tests against the phase arithmetic and they agree.
contracts.failure_mode: A stored window that fails validation is dropped and a fresh one begins; a saved version 2 window is lost once on upgrade.

summary: The code is sound. The long-frame phase arithmetic matches the worked examples in the tests. The daemon step timers are used from one goroutine each, and `Emit` cannot block the ready callback. The PostHog allowlist covers every new key, and the sanitizer re-validates entry-point and bundle names. I found four things to consider, none of them blocking. The docs say only `first` and `cold` launches carry main's steps, but `update` launches carry them too. The docs say `startup_ms` starts when the daemon process starts, but it starts at the beginning of `Run`. The steps IPC in `launchProperties` runs after the usable-wait race and the pagehide handoff, so a window closed during it loses the launch event. The `serverReused` derivation in the main-process handler has no test.
